column2: My [rumor_councillor.GetJobTitle], [rumor_councillor.GetTitledFirstName], could barely keep [rumor_councillor.GetHerHis] voice down. In a tavern, a dying sellsword babbled of a vault his company was paid to forget, and of the thing they saw inside it: a treasure out of the oldest songs of [Root.Religion.GetName], one that kings have killed for. If [rumor_councillor.GetFirstName] is right, it has lain there for centuries, waiting for a lord bold enough to claim it.

After the council meeting, [rumor_councillor.GetJobTitle] [rumor_councillor.GetFirstName] drew me aside. [rumor_councillor.GetSheHeCap] has found an old map in the margins of a temple ledger, and the map points to a shrine abandoned in the wars of my forefathers. If the stories are true, a rare treasure of [Root.Religion.GetName] was walled up there before the shrine burned.

During this evening's council, [rumor_councillor.GetJobTitle] [rumor_councillor.GetFirstName] told us what the peasants whisper: that the bones of a [Root.GetArtifactSource] lie in a forgotten barrow not far from here, and that whoever finds them will carry a little of the dead hero's virtue.
Start the search at once, [rumor_councillor.GetJobTitle]!
§Y[rumor_councillor.GetJobTitle] [rumor_councillor.GetFirstName]§! sets out at once to find the treasure, paid out of your taxes for as long as the search lasts.\n
You have my thanks, [rumor_councillor.GetFirstName]. We shall see.
You may send any of your councillors after the treasure for as long as the rumor holds.\n

[relic_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] has come home, mud to the knees, with a bundle wrapped in oilcloth. Inside lies what the barrow kept: the remains of a [Root.GetArtifactSource], and [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] swears by [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] that they are genuine. How will I reward my [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle]?

[relic_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] kneels before my seat and unwraps what [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] carried out of the burnt shrine. The treasure is real, a thing of [Root.Religion.GetName] that the priests have only seen in drawings, and now it is mine. How will I reward my [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle]?

The court falls silent as [relic_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] lays the treasure at my feet. [relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] is thinner than when [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] left, and there are scars that were not there before, but the vault was where the sellsword said, and the legend of [Root.Religion.GetName] lay inside it. Bards will sing of this day. How will I reward my [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle]?

[relic_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] has returned with grim news and a heavy chest. The treasure we sought is already in another lord's hands, or never existed at all. But the trail ended in the hoard of whoever hid it, and [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] has brought every coin home. How will I reward my [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle]?
Finding relics is what I pay [relic_hunter.GetHerHim] for!
An impressive find, but finding treasures is what I pay [relic_hunter.GetHerHim] for!
Legend or not, finding treasures is what I pay [relic_hunter.GetHerHim] for!
I will see [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is suitably rewarded.
I will see [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is richly compensated!
I will see [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] swims in gold!
[relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] has earned my favor, I suppose.
[relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] shall have my favor.
[relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] has truly earned my favor!
Everyone shall hear of [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] deeds!
Everyone shall hear of [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] impressive deeds!
Everyone shall hear of [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] legendary deeds!

[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] came to me with regrettable news. Too many years have passed since we first heard the rumor, and the trail has gone cold. Whatever lay at its end is lost to us now, and the search is over.
[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] can no longer search for the treasure. The rumor still holds, and another of my councillors may take up the trail.
Alas.
You may send another councillor after the treasure.\n
§Y[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]§! makes great progress in the search for the treasure.\n
§Y[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]§! struggles in the search for the treasure.\n

[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] approached me after the council meeting to ask for envoys. Somewhere among the courts of my neighbours there are men who know where the treasure lies, and they will only talk to someone with gifts and fine words. While my diplomats are away, the business of my own court will suffer.
You shall have your diplomats, [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle].
I cannot spare them.

The search has slowed, [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] tells me. [relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] has promising leads, but they run into wild country where beastmen, greenskins and worse haunt the roads. Without an escort taken from my levies, [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] will never come back.
We cannot miss this chance. Take the men.

My [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] wants a decree letting [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] treasure hunters search the cellars, warehouses and strongrooms of my towns. The burghers will howl, and my builders will lose the hands they need, but [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is sure that some merchant bought the trail and sits on it.
You shall have your decree, [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle].
I cannot provoke my subjects like that.

[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] has learned that [spy_target.GetTitledFirstName] of [spy_title.GetName] knows where the treasure lies, and will not say. [relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] asks for my spies to learn the secret, whatever it takes. While they are busy, my own plots and my guard against others' will suffer.
The treasure matters more. The spies are yours.

[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] has spent weeks bent over crumbling scrolls and chronicles in search of the treasure. [relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] is on the right path, but alone the work goes slowly, and [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] asks for the learned men of [primary_title.GetName] to help. Their own studies would wait.
The brightest minds of the realm are yours.

Despite the gold I set aside for the search every month, [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] says the purse is empty. Guides, bribes and mules all cost money, [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] says, and asks for more.
Very well, [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle]. You shall have it.
Empty? What a wastrel!
§Y[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]§! gets no more gold.\n
One of my spies brings disturbing news: [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] has been putting the extra gold I gave [relic_hunter.GetHerHim] into [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] own purse!
I never should have trusted that light-fingered traitor!
I shall show mercy, but I expect double the effort.
§Y[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]§! is grateful and works harder, speeding up the search a little.\n

For some time I have worried about [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]'s progress, or the lack of it. Now my fears are confirmed: through [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] carelessness the guide drowned at a ford, and with him went the only map of the trail.
Why did I trust the search to that [GetRootFromInsult]?!
The search for the treasure suffers a great setback.\n

[relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] has shared an intriguing discovery. On the trail, [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] has heard of an even rarer treasure! If we follow the new lead, some of the work done so far will still help, but the search will be longer and dearer.
How exciting! Follow the new lead.
The rumor grows greater. Half the progress made so far carries over to the new search.\n
Too risky. We stay on the trail we know.

[Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap] must have cursed my search, for I have just been brought the most dreadful news! [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName] has died on the road, far from home, while searching for the treasure.
[relic_hunter.GetFirstName] is with [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] now.
A letter from [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]: [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is making steady progress in the search for the treasure.

A letter from [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]: [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is close to the end of the trail, and the treasure should be in [relic_hunter.GetHerHis] hands within the year!

A letter from [relic_hunter.GetJobTitle] [relic_hunter.GetFirstName]: [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] has lost months following a false lead. [relic_hunter.GetSheHeCap] assures me [relic_hunter.GetSheHe] is back on the right trail.
As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they turned up a curious piece that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there. It is mine now.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they turned up a strange idol that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there. It seems to have been holy to the [original_item_owner.GetManWoman].

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they broke open a strongroom and found a treasure of great worth that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there!

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away a copy of one of my own treasures there! An obvious and shoddy forgery. It goes on the fire.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found a venerated object of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName] that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there. The defenders fought hard for it.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found a venerated object of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName] that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there, and they threw it on the pyre with the defenders who fought for it.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found a treasure of legend that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there! Songs will be sung of this day.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away a copy of one of my greatest treasures there! An obvious and shoddy forgery. It goes on the fire.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found a holy relic of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName] that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there. Scores of defenders died around it rather than let it go.

As my troops ransacked the [target_title.GetHolding] of [target_title.GetName], they found a holy relic of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName] that [original_item_owner.GetTitledFirstName] had hidden away there. Scores of defenders died around it. It burned all the same.
Wonderful news!
Hmm, interesting.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] be praised!
It will go nicely in my collection.
At last it is held by someone truly worthy!
It will be the centerpiece of my collection!
One less imitation to worry about!
That will teach them!
This heretical imitation will plague the world no more!
Let it be known that I am the scourge of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName]!

[original_item_owner.Religion.GetHighGodName] knows what blasphemy they will subject it to.

[looter.GetHerHisCap] troops also found one of the great relics of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName], and the godless brutes threw it on the fire!
Oh no...
The thieving scum!
The barbarian scum!
How dare the bastard touch it with [looter.GetHerHis] unworthy hands?!
Oh, the shame is unbearable!
But... mine was clearly the original!
Have they no respect for the divine?!
What... what has [looter.GetSheHe] done?!
This is an affront to all of [original_item_owner.Religion.GetName]!
